question:
A block of mass 1 kg is dropped from the top of a building of height X m. What will be the value of X if the block hits the ground with a velocity of 20 m/s?

(Take the value of g = 10 {m/s}² )
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The motion of the block can be described using the **Equations of Motion** formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton**. These equations relate displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time for an object moving with constant acceleration.
 
• In this problem, the block is "dropped," which implies that its **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**. The height from which it is dropped is **X**, and it hits the ground with a **final velocity (v)** of **20 m/s**.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** acting on the block is given as **10 m/s²**. Since the motion is downward, the acceleration is positive in the direction of displacement.
 
• To find the height **X**, we use the **Third Equation of Motion**: **v² = u² + 2as**, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, **a** is the acceleration, and **s** is the displacement (height **X**).
